summary: iOS capture shows the on-screen swipe/gesture keyboard tutorial overlay and a simulated keyboard area, which is not part of the form-field component and shouldn't appear in the snapshot.

Map the native iOS label font to the same weight/letter-spacing used in the React design tokens (bold + tightened tracking).
Standardize the error-state border width and asterisk spacing via shared design tokens across platforms.
Add a visual-regression guard that fails when native keyboard/tutorial artifacts exceed N% of the captured canvas.
intentional: The iOS device canvas is 1170x2532 vs React 342x296, so absolute pixel-perfect match is impossible; differences are expected to be density-scaled rather than identical.

Disable or suppress native soft keyboard and tutorial overlay during Slock visual capture, or capture both ends in identical states (keyboard hidden) for parity.
Strip or hide the text caret in static visual-test rendering to avoid non-semantic caret diffs between platforms.
Unify keyboard-avoidance / safe-area logic in the KuiklyFormField container so vertical layout is consistent when the keyboard is present.
Ensure the Server Name error state uses identical border color, border thickness, and message typography/weight on Android and iOS.
intentional: Text caret visible only on focused iOS field may be considered platform-typical

summary: Keyboard is visible in the iOS capture but absent in the React baseline, occupying the lower half of the canvas and reducing visible component area.
Error-state textarea on iOS has visibly different vertical proportions (shorter height) compared to the React baseline, suggesting different minRows or padding-top/bottom.
iOS error textarea has lighter, more saturated pink/red fill versus a much paler tint on React.
Error helper text on iOS appears in a lighter red-orange weight, while React uses a deeper red and bolder weight for 'Agreement body must be shorter.'
Text caret position differs: iOS places the cursor at the very start of the first character while React shows no caret / different insertion point.
likelyCauses: iOS capture was taken while the soft keyboard was focused, scaling the layout and shifting component bounds.
Different default font metrics between iOS (San Francisco) and the React web baseline cause line-height and textarea height to diverge.
Error-state background color tokens are not aligned between platforms (different red-tint values).
Helper/counter text typography tokens (color, weight) differ between React and iOS implementations.
suggestedFixes: Dismiss the keyboard (tapping outside the field) before capturing the iOS screenshot, or capture with focus elsewhere to match baseline framing.
Equalize textarea minRows, line-height, and vertical padding across platforms so error-state heights match at the same content.
Align error-state background fill token between iOS and React (same red-tint hex/opacity).
Normalize helper and counter text color/weight tokens for error state across platforms.
Verify caret/insertion indicator styling on iOS UITextView vs. the React textarea to ensure consistent rendering.

summary: Checkbox rows render identically in both React and iOS renderings — checked, unchecked, and disabled states all present with matching label text, checkbox fill, and check mark glyph.
Checkbox box size, border thickness, and check stroke weight appear visually consistent between the two sides.
Label typography (font, weight, size) for 'As Task selected', 'Permission row unchecked', and 'Disabled checked' matches across platforms.
Disabled state color treatment (muted gray fill and label) matches between React and iOS.
Vertical spacing between the three checkbox rows is consistent across both renderings.
likelyCauses: Minor pixel-level differences driven by iOS native rendering of checkbox borders and antialiasing versus the React web baseline.
Subtle font hinting/metrics differences between the system fonts used on iOS and the web font stack in the React baseline.
suggestedFixes: Confirm the small pixel mismatch (~0.98%) is within acceptable tolerance and attribute it to platform rendering rather than a regression.
If tighter parity is desired, normalize the disabled-state opacity and border color tokens to identical values on both platforms.
Verify the iOS Checkbox component references the same design tokens (size, corner radius, check stroke) as the React Raft UI Checkbox.
Snapshot only the cropped component region (342×132) for both sides to remove canvas-size scaling artifacts from comparison metrics.
intentional: Differences in canvas dimensions (React 342×132 element-bounds crop vs iOS full 1170×2532 screen) are an artifact of the comparison harness, not a UI divergence.
Platform-specific font rendering (iOS San Francisco vs web font stack) is expected and typically acceptable.

summary: Three checkbox states (checked, unchecked, disabled) render isomorphic across Android and iOS — text content, checkbox shapes, and color treatments match.
Title 'Raft UI Checkbox' and labels appear identical in weight, size, and alignment between sides.
Canvas size differs (baseline 342×396 manual crop vs iOS full 1170×2532), but component-bounds crop on baseline contains the same three rows shown on iOS, so the comparison region is aligned.
High pixel-perfect similarity (99.37%) and low mismatch (0.63%) confirm no structural divergence in the rendered checkbox states.
likelyCauses: Differences are limited to per-platform canvas sizing and framing (cropped component-bounds on baseline vs full device viewport on iOS) rather than component-level rendering.
suggestedFixes: No component fix required — checkbox states are visually isomorphic; mark as pass.
If tighter parity is desired, normalize the comparison canvas so the baseline uses the same full-viewport size as the current side to avoid extra whitespace.
Document the intentional canvas size difference so future regressions aren't flagged against framing rather than the component itself.
intentional: Android baseline image is cropped to component bounds (342×396) while iOS uses the full 1170×2532 viewport — this is a harness framing choice, not a UI divergence.

summary: React baseline uses a much heavier/bolder font weight for the checkbox labels compared to the iOS render, which uses a noticeably lighter/thinner weight.
Vertical spacing between the three check items appears slightly tighter on iOS, while the gap between the last item and the bottom edge is larger on iOS.
The yellow circle marker on iOS renders slightly smaller in diameter and with a thinner stroke than the React baseline.
Check glyph (tick) inside the filled square on iOS appears marginally thinner than the React version.
No missing elements; structure, colors, and alignment match across both renders.
likelyCauses: iOS SwiftUI/SwiftUIKit default font weight differs from the React/CSS bold font applied in the design system.
Marker SVG/asset on iOS uses a different size or stroke-width constant than the web asset.
Minor padding/token mismatch between web spacing tokens and iOS layout constants.
Antialiasing and scale differences when rendering the small vector markers on a 3x retina canvas.
suggestedFixes: Apply the design system's bold/medium font weight token to the check label Text style on iOS.
Verify the circle marker asset's diameter and stroke-width against the web design tokens and update if needed.
Align iOS vertical spacing tokens (inter-item and bottom padding) with the web values.
Re-snapshot with ignoreAntialiasing tolerance reviewed, and confirm the tick glyph stroke matches the web asset.
Optionally add a design-token lint step that compares web and iOS rendered values for the same component.
intentional: Resolution and device-scale differences between the 342×112 web capture and the 1170×2532 iOS capture are expected and not a defect.
The thin font weight on iOS may be an intentional platform default; confirm with design before changing.

summary: Layout/content is isomorphic: same three check states (square checked, square unchecked, circle yellow) render with identical labels and ordering on both platforms.
iOS renders the component cluster in the top-left of a much taller canvas (1170×2532) versus Android's compact 342×112 frame, but the component bounds themselves appear consistent.
Typography weight, glyph shapes, marker geometry, and colors (black square, yellow circle with black check) are visually equivalent between Android and iOS.
likelyCauses: Resolution/canvas size difference is intrinsic to platform DPI (Android 1026×336 reference vs iOS 1170×2532 full device canvas); no crop was applied on iOS side.
iOS canvas is uncropped, so most of the mismatch area is empty whitespace rather than component divergence.
suggestedFixes: Apply a component-bounds crop on the iOS side (analogous to the Android manual-rect crop) so the comparison is over the actual check-marker component area rather than the full device canvas.
Re-run the diff with both crops matched; the 0.48% pixel mismatch is dominated by empty canvas padding and is not a real visual divergence.
No code change required for the check-marker component itself unless the cropped diff still reports differences.
intentional: Different canvas dimensions per platform reflect native device viewport sizes.
Empty whitespace below the component on iOS is expected when not cropping to component bounds.

likelyCauses: Comparison canvas for iOS was not cropped to the element bounds, unlike the React baseline which used contract 'component-bounds'.

Normalize the iOS canvas background to remove the empty area beneath the component to focus pixel comparison on the rendered UI.
Verify font metrics for the AttentionDot labels on iOS align with the design system specs used in React.

summary: Android progress bars are noticeably shorter in length than React baseline, leaving extra empty space on the right
Both 'Downloading update' and 'Verifying package' bars share the same reduction in width on Android
Labels, percentages, and fill colors are visually consistent between the two implementations
Outer border around the entire Android card is present while React baseline does not show one
The Android version also appears to include a faint yellow/cream background tint that React does not have
likelyCauses: Android ProgressBar component likely uses WRAP_CONTENT or does not stretch to fill available horizontal space
Missing layout constraint (e.g., missing match_parent / 0dp in ConstraintLayout or layout_weight in LinearLayout)
Possible difference in default parent container width or padding between the two platforms
The additional Android card border and tinted background suggest different storybook/test wrapper styling between RN and Android harnesses
suggestedFixes: Set the ProgressBar's width to match_parent (or use 0dp with start/end constraints) inside a match_parent parent
Wrap the ProgressBar in a container with a fixed/full width and ensure horizontal sizing matches the React reference
Normalize the storybook/preview container styling so border and background tint match across platforms
Verify scale-independent dimensions (dp vs px) so Android width equals React width at the same canvas size
Add a visual regression tolerance for progress-bar fill width in the design-system test suite

summary: Progress bars, labels, and percentages render with matching typography, colors (pink #64%, cyan #28%), and bar fills on both sides.
iOS canvas (1170×2532) includes substantial empty space below the two progress bars; React snapshot (342×124) is tightly cropped to the component bounds.
iOS contents are not vertically anchored to the bottom of its canvas, leaving a large blank region beneath the component group; React is tightly element-cropped.
Both sides show identical label text ("Downloading update", "Verifying package"), percentages, and bar height/border styling.
likelyCauses: Slock baseline crop uses element/component-bounds (targetRect = full 342×124) while iOS used no crop (current.crop = null), so the comparison viewport differs dramatically in size.
iOS test renderer did not constrain content to the component bounds, producing an oversized canvas with whitespace.
Possible missing SafeArea/padding constraints or auto-layout sizing in the iOS test harness.
suggestedFixes: Configure the iOS snapshot test to crop to component bounds (mirror React's element contract) so canvases match.
Add a fixed-height container or compress vertical content so the iOS component occupies only its intrinsic bounds.
In SwiftUI / UIKit, ensure the progress-bar view uses intrinsicContentSize or a tight frame to avoid expanding whitespace.
Include a harness-level option to set `scale`/`resize` to a comparable dimension before diffing.
If the whitespace is expected (e.g., full-screen test target), update tolerance/contract documentation so reviewers know it's intentional.
intentional: Label text, percentage values, bar fill widths (64%, 28%), colors, and stroke styling appear intentionally identical.
Typography weight/size and label-to-bar spacing match between platforms.

summary: Android shows the progress bar group inside a cropped/inset 342×124 component-bounds region, while iOS renders against a full 1170×2532 device canvas — the iOS frame extends to a large empty area below the bars.
Header, labels, percentages, track outline, fill widths (64% and 28%), and fill colors (pink/cyan) render identically on both ends after normalising for scale.
Text glyphs appear slightly thicker/heavier on iOS, consistent with platform font-weight defaults (San Francisco vs Roboto fallback).
Bar outlines on Android look fractionally heavier pixel-for-pixel because the baseline canvas was upscaled compared to the native iOS stroke; the underlying dp stroke is the same.
likelyCauses: Baseline image was manually cropped to component bounds (342×124) while iOS baseline was captured at full device resolution, so the surround area differs even though the component itself does not.
Minor font rendering differences between the two platform text engines (iOS SF vs Android Roboto/equivalent).
Stroke weight difference is an artefact of up-sampling the small Android crop rather than a real dp mismatch.
suggestedFixes: Compare using a matching crop strategy on iOS (component-bounds) so the two images cover the same logical region.
Run the comparison after scaling both canvases to the same dp grid, or down-scale the iOS capture to the Android baseline before diffing.
If the per-platform font default is intentional, keep it; otherwise pin a single text style (fontFamily + fontWeight) on the progress-bar component to neutralise glyph weight drift.
intentional: Platform font weight / glyph shape differences between iOS SF and Android Roboto.
Background area below the bars on iOS is unused and intentionally blank.

summary: Channel suggestion list is anchored to the top of the viewport in iOS instead of sitting above the composer as in React, leaving a large empty gap between the suggestions and the composer bar.
iOS render includes the full iOS keyboard (QWERTY + autocomplete bar '|', 'The', 'I'm' and a blue 'send' key) consuming the lower half of the screen; the React baseline has no keyboard visible.

Selected suggestion row ('design — Product and UI decisions') uses the same pink highlight in both, but in iOS the pink row extends the full container width with no inner gutter, while React keeps a small left/right padding.

Composer bar in iOS is compressed vertically and its action icons (image-plus, paperclip, 'As Task' checkbox, send arrow) appear smaller and more tightly packed than in React, where icons are larger and more spaced.

likelyCauses: iOS snapshot is a full-screen device capture (1170×2532) rather than an element-bounds crop, so it includes the system keyboard and surrounding chrome that the React baseline intentionally excludes.
The iOS channel-suggestions component is laid out against the safe area / keyboard insets and pinned to the top, whereas the React version is docked directly above the composer.
Different default font metrics and icon sizing between the React web stack and the iOS native implementation for the composer controls.
No outset/crop defined for the iOS baseline, so the comparison canvas includes uncompared background pixels driving the 38.8% mismatch.
suggestedFixes: Add a matching element-bounds crop (or outset) for the iOS capture so the keyboard and empty viewport are excluded from the diff, or hide the keyboard during visual-test capture.
Reposition the iOS channel suggestions so they sit flush above the composer bar (same vertical relationship as React) rather than pinned to the top of the screen.
Match the composer's icon size, spacing, and '#' glyph weight to the React baseline, or update the React baseline as the new intentional design and regenerate golden snapshots.
Tighten the selected-row highlight padding so the pink fill has consistent horizontal insets matching the React reference.
Re-run Slock capture after layout fixes and confirm pixel-perfect similarity rises above ~0.95 before closing the regression.
intentional: Pink selection highlight on the active 'design' suggestion appears intentional and is consistent across both platforms.
Presence of the autocomplete suggestion bar ('I / The / I'm') above the iOS keyboard is iOS system UI and not part of the app component.

summary: The React baseline shows a full Create Agent dialog with a prominent peachy/coral warning banner ('Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more') and the complete form including Model, Reasoning, and Mode sections ending with a 'Fast mode' checkbox.

The iOS view is obscured at the bottom by the iOS system keyboard, hiding the Model dropdown contents, the Reasoning field, the Mode/Fast mode checkbox, and all footer/CTA buttons that are visible in the React baseline.
Vertical spacing/padding between form fields (Computer→Name→Description→Runtime) is visibly tighter in iOS; labels sit closer to their inputs compared to the React baseline.
The 'Suggested computer: computer-mbp' helper text present beneath the Computer select in iOS has no counterpart in the React baseline.
likelyCauses: iOS screenshot was captured with the on-screen keyboard up during form interaction (likely while editing Description), causing lower fields to be hidden.
The Create Agent iOS implementation may not be rendering the agent-limit warning banner / quota alert component that exists in the React version.
Different vertical spacing/density tokens or layout constraints used between React web and iOS native form rendering.
iOS scroll offset places the top of the form at a different y-position so the banner area scrolls above the viewport.

suggestedFixes: Dismiss the iOS keyboard before capturing the screenshot (or capture a non-focused state) so all form fields and CTAs are visible.
Verify the iOS dialog renders the agent-limit/quota warning banner; add the equivalent component if missing on native.
Normalize vertical spacing between form fields and labels to match the React baseline tokens.
Ensure the iOS form scrolls so that when the keyboard appears, the active field stays in view without hiding required later fields; consider keyboardAvoidingView equivalent.
Add a stable visual-regression baseline for iOS using a keyboard-dismissed state to avoid spurious differences.
intentional: iOS system keyboard overlay rendering is platform-native and expected.

summary: React baseline shows a pink/cream 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more' banner directly below the 'CREATE AGENT' header; Android current does not show this limit-reached banner at all.

Android implementation adds an extra suggested-computer hint element not present in the React spec.

Missing or different scroll container/scale settings on Android: scale-to-fit or different padding/scale causes fields to render smaller and the Cancel/Create Agent buttons to become visible rather than scrolled-off.
Unit/density differences (dp vs px) and layout compression make Android content fit where React content overflows.
suggestedFixes: Add the same 'Agent limit reached (2/2 on Free plan). Upgrade for more' warning banner component in Android, conditionally rendered when the user is on the Free plan with 2/2 agents, matching color, weight and copy of the React version.
Remove the 'Suggested computer: computer-mbp' helper text from the Android COMPUTER field if it is not part of the design, or add it to the React baseline if it is intended.

Match React layout/scroll behavior: keep Cancel and Create Agent either pinned in a sticky footer or outside the scrollable form so the Reason field isn't pushed off-screen; do not auto-scale the form down to force buttons into view.

Align vertical spacing between form fields and labels with the React baseline (increase dp padding between sections) so COMPUTER→NAME→DESCRIPTION→RUNTIME→PROVIDER→MODEL→REASONING gaps are visually consistent.

intentional: Android dialog composites the form and action buttons within a single viewport rather than letting the form overflow, which may be an intentional responsive choice but conflicts with React's behavior.

summary: React shows a single two-column layout (Connected Apps header + filters on top, full-width cards below) while Android reorganizes into multiple stacked sections (Connected Apps, Built-in, Marketplace) with repeated Marketplace/Installed/My apps counters rendered twice as stat tiles and again as icon+label tabs.

React has a single 'Register app' button in the header next to the 'EXPERIMENTAL' badge; Android places '+ Register app' inside the 'Third-party apps for this server' card and removes the header-level placement.
Android adds leading emoji-style icons (link icon, package icon, eye/checkmark/key icons) next to section headers and tabs; React uses plain text labels only.

Android renders stat numbers (3, 2, 1) as large prominent digits with truncated labels ('Marketpla…'); React renders 'Marketplace 3 / Installed 2 / My apps 1' as flat pill buttons with no large numerals.

GitHub card in React shows a yellow square avatar with 'GI' plus a green 'BUILT-IN' badge and a separate 'Open' pink button; Android collapses avatar+badge into text, merges description lines ('Available to all users & agents · Built-in source control integration. · github.com') and prefixes the 'Open' button with an external-link icon.

Stat-counter component was repurposed into both large tiles and small icon-tabs on Android, creating duplicate affordances not present in the React spec.

Section header icons were added on Android (emoji/icons) without a corresponding design update on React.
suggestedFixes: Unify spacing/padding tokens between React and Android; Android cards appear too tight — increase vertical padding to match React card rhythm.
Remove the duplicate Marketplace/Installed/My apps rendering on Android; keep one variant (either the large stat tiles or the icon-tab row) and align with React's flat-pill style.
Restore the 'Install' primary CTA on marketplace cards on Android; 'Details' should be a secondary text/icon action, not a replacement.
Remove emoji-style section icons on Android, or add equivalent ones in React for parity; standardize header icon usage across platforms.
Restore the 'BUILT-IN' badge and avatar square on the GitHub card on Android and avoid inlining description metadata into a single paragraph.

Logo image uses different intrinsic height/aspect ratio on Android, affecting surrounding spacing.
Shared design tokens not fully applied — per-platform padding/spacing values diverge.

Share spacing constants via the design system so header-to-logo and logo-to-heading gaps match React baseline.
Normalize SafeArea handling so both implementations reserve the same top offset.
Lock logo container to a fixed size on Android to prevent vertical drift from intrinsic image measurement.

summary: iOS keyboard is visible and covers the lower portion of the screen (Google/GitHub buttons, Terms text, Forgot Password, Create One links), whereas React shows the full layout

likelyCauses: iOS keyboard appearance not accounted for in the test harness layout (no `adjustResize` / safe-area insets applied)

Add safe-area insets to the bottom of the auth screen so footer links are not occluded
Align reference canvas/dimensions for visual testing to compare like-for-like

summary: iOS side shows an on-screen keyboard covering the lower half of the login form, while Android side has no keyboard present (scroll content visible: Terms/Privacy, Forgot Password, Create One).

Email and Password input text appears cropped on the left edge on iOS (cursor/text clipped at input border), but fully contained on Android.

likelyCauses: iOS platform is showing the software keyboard while Android renders without one, indicating differing default input focus/keyboard presentation between ends.
Adaptive resize / keyboard-avoiding view behavior not being applied identically across platforms (iOS shrinks viewport, Android does not).
Different safe-area or system-bar offset handling between ends when keyboard is raised.
Possible missing dismissKeyboard or focus state synchronization in the Kuikly render on the iOS side.
suggestedFixes: Dismiss the keyboard or blur inputs before capture on iOS so both renders show equivalent viewport state for diffing.
Apply platform-consistent keyboardAvoidingView / softKeyboardMode so layout reflows identically and does not occlude bottom controls.
Ensure Email/Password input paddings and text insets match across platforms to avoid left-edge clipping.
Normalize header tag pill (ANDROID/iOS) and safe-area insets in the test scaffold only, not in product code, so it does not affect comparisons.
Re-run the comparison after equalizing keyboard state on both ends to verify whether residual layout differences remain.
intentional: Platform-specific software keyboard is expected behavior on iOS, but it should be controlled during visual regression capture.

cases.title: Thread Message Row Long Inline Code

declaredDivergences.description: Chip fill/border paint past the glyphs without reserving the box width in layout, so the border-to-neighbor gap approximates React's inline-block advance (atomic box rewrite tracked as task #448).
Long inline code wraps via the shared zero-width-space bridge (slockInlineCodeCharWrapBridgeThreshold), not native char-level wrap (task #401 A-bridge).

summary: iOS (right) renders body text noticeably larger and with wider line-height than React (left), causing the same content to consume more vertical space and clip/truncate earlier in the available width.

Inline-code chip backgrounds on iOS (e.g., the long path, the ./gradlew command, raft.build.markdown.inlineCode) wrap differently — iOS preserves the trailing glyph before the closing chip border while React consistently shows a closing black frame after each wrapped segment; several iOS chips appear to be missing their right-side frame on wrap.

The yellow inline-code fill on iOS bleeds across whitespace between adjacent code spans (e.g., 'inlineCode' and 'go test ./...' and 'git commit -s' appear to share a single continuous yellow box), whereas React keeps each code span as a separate bordered chip.

Header metadata row differs: iOS shows the avatar, name, and a truncated 'Keeps visual testing…' subtitle on one line with the timestamp appended, while React stacks the avatar/name line and uses a more compact, two-line header with 'Keeps vis…' truncation and the timestamp on its own sub-line; vertical alignment of the avatar relative to the name differs slightly between the two.

Body text wrapping on iOS causes the long inline-code path to overflow the right edge of the container (final glyphs clip at the container border) instead of breaking cleanly inside the chip like React does.
likelyCauses: iOS text engine uses a larger default body font size or line-height multiplier than the React baseline.
iOS TextKit/UIKit wraps inline-code chips on a per-glyph basis and omits the trailing border on continuation lines, and may merge backgrounds of adjacent inline spans separated by spaces.
Missing or different `word-break`/`overflow-wrap` settings for inline code in iOS markdown renderer, allowing tokens to exceed container width instead of soft-wrapping mid-token.
iOS message row header layout uses a single-line HStack rather than the multi-line header layout in React, changing avatar/name/timestamp stacking.
suggestedFixes: Set iOS body font size and line-height to match React's MessageItem body metrics (verify against the 390×844 baseline).
Fix inline-code chip rendering on iOS to (a) preserve the black right/bottom border on each wrap line and (b) not merge backgrounds across whitespace-separated spans.
Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (or equivalent `lineBreakMode`/hyphenation setting) to inline-code runs so long tokens wrap inside the chip rather than clipping at the container edge.
Align the message-row header layout between platforms so avatar/name and timestamp/subtitle stack consistently.

Consider a follow-up to verify React does not regress after iOS fixes; revisit the known intentional divergences list if any of the chip-merge / border fixes affect bare #number or @mention rendering.

cases.title: Settings Administration Full Height Screen

summary: Android renders a full top app bar with back arrow and 'Administration' title that is absent on the React baseline.

Android displays more vertical sections (System Channels, Pending Invites, Join Links, Pre-Join Agreement, Onboarding, Translation, Member Permissions, Sidebar Order, Danger Zone) with distinct card-based groupings versus React's flat single-column form layout.

React uses pink/red filled primary buttons (Update Role, Save, Create Invite Link) while Android replaces them with yellow/gold accent buttons and outline-style action chips (Required/Disabled, Yes/No, Hide Humans/Visible).

React shows form inputs as native dropdowns (Select member..., Admin, @cindy (Cindy)) with mm/dd/yyyy date input; Android renders information as labeled rows with leading icon tiles and 'Unavailable'/'Last owner' status text on the right.
Character counter on Android ('81/5000 characters') and Preview block placement differ from React's preview rendering and placement of '81/5000' inline under textarea.
likelyCauses: React baseline and Android implementation diverge from a shared design system; Android is using a newer visual language (tile-based cards, yellow accent, monospace metadata) not reflected in React's flat form.
Primary button color token mismatch: React uses destructive/pink, Android uses brand yellow.
State indicators (toggle on/off, required/disabled) implemented as pill chips on Android vs. checkboxes on React, indicating inconsistent component mapping.
Section grouping on Android uses cards with headers while React relies on whitespace separators.
Header/navigation component (app bar with back arrow) is present in Android native shell but missing from React web render.
suggestedFixes: Reconcile section header style and grouping (cards vs. flat) across platforms; align typography weight, size, and uppercase tracking.
Standardize primary action button color token; pick pink or yellow as the canonical primary and update the other platform.
Unify state indicator components: map React checkboxes to Android toggle pills consistently and share the same active/inactive styling.
Add the top app bar with back navigation to the React web Administration screen to match Android.
Normalize Pending Invites row metadata (Invited by, timestamps) and action button placement.
intentional: Different overall canvas height (2564 vs 2647) likely reflects native scrollbar/status bar differences and may be acceptable.
